no_rows.reason: field_bool with no set_limits, set_hard_limits or custom handler: server-schema.cpp:572 stores the boolean verbatim (val = data.at(n).get<bool>()), so the accepted value is identity, and generation_settings carries no 'verbose' key at all (server-task.cpp to_json lists stream at 73/127 and timings_per_token at 82/141, nothing else of these four). Live: {"verbose": true} -> 200 (verbose_true.json, sha 87191e9f...) with no __verbose in the native /completion body and no generation_settings.verbose; the __verbose field only appears on OpenAI-compatible responses (oai_verbose.out, sha 2dcde335...). Sending {"verbose": 1} -> 400 "Field 'verbose': [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be boolean, but is number" (verbose_num.json, sha 7b6e156e...), a type error with no bounds, so it matches neither the effective nor the reject rule.

field_bool identity: server-schema.cpp:572 assigns the sent boolean verbatim, and generation_settings.timings_per_token (server-task.cpp:82 and :141) then reports exactly that value. Live: {"timings_per_token": true} -> 200 with generation_settings.timings_per_token = true (tpt_true.json, sha dc5df906...), equal to the value sent, while the field-omitted base request reports false (base.json, sha 55b11fdd...). The effective rule needs a value different from both the sent value and the omitted-field default, which a boolean identity assignment cannot produce; false is the default and true is the sent value. Sending {"timings_per_token": 1} -> 400 "Field 'timings_per_token': [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be boolean, but is number" (tpt_num.json, sha 28d4cc69...), a type error with no bounds.
